docs.text: Audio Design Showcase While not formerly trained through any specific institution, audio remains one of my strongest and most passionate skillsets in my professional career. An upbringing of highschool performance art combined with a love of detail gave me a well trained ear for the experience of sound, which in my years at university turned into a skill I had a knack for in game development. Each audio file provided is the same used in the final project they were made for. 28 Leicester Square (August 2025 - April 2026) I handled and organized everything to do with sound in this project. That included: Production spreadsheet of every needed sfx (approved by our project lead) Designs of the sounds themselves Recording, Sampling, & foley work Audio balancing both in and out of engine Audio implementation (+ variation & pitch shifting) Custom audio system framework (Engineering showcase) Music composition and production (Music showcase) This project was the first to truly let me practice audio as a sole focus, instead of it being relegated to a skillset I had to leave on the backburner until the project "called for it" (which was often just moments before the final deadline). As such, the project stands as the single best reference point for my audio design skillset. Out of everything in the project, around 60-70% of the original sound samples were either recorded or digitally generated by me. The rest were pulled from existing samples found on freesound.org. By the end of the project, I had made around 80+ finalized sound effects for the final game. -Ambience- The two ambience tracks are where the game gets most of its atmosphere. The first one here is the general ambience, an 8 minute loop that plays regardless of position. Interspersed are random bits of foley mostly from a general soundpack I had access to, along side some occasional drone samples I had lying around that are themselves unnerving to listen to. LS-GeneralAmbience.ogg If you stand by the windows, you can hear the outdoor ambience, which done by positionally moving the audio player around to the closest window in 3D space. Combining this with the general ambience in-game leads to some nice layering, I think. LS-WindowAMB.ogg As a bonus, at the start of the game is a very important table that the designers struggled to properly get playtesters to notice. So, I thought it would be fun to have the radio on that table play some old music from around the time period. Even if it's a really minor part of the final project, it was a fun easter egg that I spent a decent amount of time researching and hunting for; The following is a nearly century year old recording of Love's Old Sweet song, public domain, filtered through an EQ I balanced to properly sell the effect of the radio. LovesOSSradio -Doors- Each door had 2 opening samples, alongside 2 closing samples, allowing for some light variation. I recorded the samples myself, taking advantage of the fact that my apartment building was legally a historical building , and consequentially hundreds of years old, giving me plenty of wiggle room to emphasis how 'not modern' the doors were. DoorOpen1.wav DoorOpen2.wav DoorClose1.wav DoorClose2.wav Additionally I made samples for struggling against a door when using wrong items on them, and a key unlocking sample for when using a correct key. DoorFail.wav UnlockDoor.wav -UI- I mostly relied on pitch shifting to give these samples variation. Inventory sounds were made via a simple synth in my DAW. InventoryIn.wav InventoryOut.wav Menu sounds I made by layering samples of myself taking sharp breaths over each other and cranking up the reverb + some light EQ balancing to emphasis the low frequencies. This approach is inspired somewhat by FromSoft's UI sounds as seen in Darksouls. MenuIn.wav MenuOut.wav -Foley interactions- The game revolves around finding 3 particular objects to open the lab. As such, I felt it was important that each of those objects had a distinct sound for picking up and placing them. Each were made from foley samples I recorded. SaltPickup.wav PlantInteract.wav BottleInteract.wav -Monster sfx- I ended up making a total of 23 unique sfx for the monsters, including variations. Each sample was sourced by friends both on & off the project making unholy noises into their microphones for me. Not displayed here due to sheer quantity, but you can hear them in the final game. -Puzzle Sfx- Puzzle solve and Puzzle Fail jingles, respectively. These were just made with a piano midi to echo the main motif. LS-PuzzleComplete.wav LS-PuzzleFailure.wav We needed a way to signify when a door was unlocked by a puzzle's completion, so using my ancient apartment doors again I somehow edited this gear sound together. I think I recorded myself twisting a doorknob, and then turned that into a midi instrument? Something like that. GearsUnlock.wav SPIN-MECH FURY (July 2026) As this was a weeklong game jam project, sound was put off until the last few hours as we were more focused on gameplay for a majority of development. On that front, I generated some simple sounds using while Jayliriah handled music. Our game was supposed to feel shovel-ware-ish, so I found it fit to just make everything synth based. With that in mind, there's not much to really show off; with only about 10 sounds in total in the project, a couple even left unused. Enjoy the following collection of my favorites. (Light audio warning as these are basically raw samples that were balanced in engine) Charge.wav DASH.wav Jumppad.wav Bumper.wav Explode.wav Other projects? While the walk down memory lane would be fun, any projects pre-capstone (Before Leicester) aren't up to the same standard of quality I hold myself to now, and as such I don't see it fit to include them here. I am also actively working on a particular, larger scale side project in my freetime. While sound hasn't been a focus for it yet, it will be soon, and I will likely include some of those samples here.

docs.text: Music Production showcase Music is incredibly special to me. I've always been drawn to it, in some way. I play the piano specifically because I like to express feelings on it, effectively self taught in its ways, removed from any official instruction. I don't play to recount existing ideas on sheet music or to impress people with my skill. I experiment, refine, and express my ideas on those keys, simply because it makes me feel heard. Of course, I'm also heavily invested in game development. Music is a fun skill to have in that context, and games are very good place to draw motivation from. So over the last 8 years or so, I have familiarized myself with the digital tools and techniques necessary to make that music (which consequentially gave me a good starting point for my sound design aspirations). Over time, that effort to 'practice' my craft eventually turned into all of this. Each audio file provided is the same used in the final project they were made for. 28 Leicester Square (August 2025 - April 2026) I handled and organized everything to do with sound in this project. That included composing & producing the original music used in the final game. The game only really required one track for the title (as the main gameplay was largely more occupied with ambience), which you can hear below. A shortened version of this theme is used for the final cutscene and credits sequence. The theme itself centers around a call & response pattern between the piano melody and the bells. The choice of strings was intentionally chosen to be reminiscent of the strings used in Project Zomboid's soundtrack, as they evoke this sort of "corrupt" feeling. Overall, I wanted this track to evoke a sort of classic, even somewhat campy horror feeling, leaning on the harmonic 7th and instrumentation to carry that feeling throughout the piece. What Hydes In the Doctor.ogg I additionally made a shorter, more sped up version of this theme for the trailer. This one gives more of an anticipatory feeling compared to the original track, which leaned more towards a feeling of tragedy originally. While putting together the trailer I made a point to match the pacing to this track as well as I could. LS_Trailer2(shorter).ogg A Werewolf is a Werewolf (Spring 2025) This is a simpler track made over the span of a weekend for my team's Alt game project. For this short little puzzle game, we needed a simple track that could loop indefinitely over the full experience. So, my overall goal was to convey that sense of unease that comes from being in the wrong place at the worst time, while also being catchy enough to hum along with while you push around block puzzles. The delay effect on the piano especially sells this, I think. Looking back, I think I would use an EQ more on the horns to cut out those harder frequencies and make it slightly less ear piercing. Light volume warning, because of that. Lunanine.mp3 Pillow Fight: Siege of the Sectional (Fall 2024) While the game itself suffers the most by far from student project syndrome, I'm still proud of how the music came together for this one even if it's on a technical level unpolished in a few ways. Since the core idea was that you were a kid living out a dream of being a powerful wizard, and we had scrapped ideas of there being a "wizard cartoon" the kid watched before falling asleep, my overall goal with this track was to balance a feeling of childlike whimsy and imagination alongside raw unfiltered heroism . On top of that, the game is centered around surviving the onslaught for exactly 5 minutes. So, I designed the song to get increasingly more intense the closer that 5 minute mark got. The result is a track that is somewhat on the longer end, so feel free to skip around on this one. SiegeOfTheSectional.mp3 Other works I have a decent pile of other personal work that isn't tied to any of these finished works. Some are just ideas, some I have eventual plans for. As a fun bonus, here's a track I arranged sometime in 2024 entirely based off a piano piece of mine of the same name (just with a few extra instruments). While itself a bit outdated at this point, I think it's a really good example of the type of music I want to be making for games. Pieces that communicate feelings that words could not dream of describing. Forgotton Forest.mp3 Many of my personal tracks also have direct story connotations to each other, this one being no exception. Connections that can be heard through shared scales, keys, melodies, progressions, ect. Sadly, most of my official work has only been in the context of projects that needed a single track. But if I ever get the proper chance to compose a full soundtrack for a game, you can expect that soundtrack to be woven into a complex tapestry of interconnected ideas reflective of the game it is intrinsically linked to.
